title: Properness and regular integral geometry of homogeneous Borel quotients
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $F$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $H\subseteq G$ be a smooth connected closed subgroup [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Let $p:G\to X$ be a quotient in the sense of [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient]: it is faithfully flat and of finite presentation, two test-scheme points have the same image exactly when their ratio lies in $H$, and all points lift fpqc locally. Then $G$ and $X$ are smooth geometrically integral $F$-schemes and regular Noetherian schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme]; geometrically integral means integral after every extension of $F$, and Noetherian means admitting a finite cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. The morphism $p$ is smooth, and for every point $x\in X$ and every field extension $L/\kappa(x)$ the fibre $G\times_X\operatorname{Spec}L$ is nonempty and integral. If $H$ is maximal among smooth connected solvable closed subgroups of $G$, then $X$ is proper over $F$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Here solvable means that the iterated scheme-theoretic commutator subgroup eventually becomes trivial; the commutator subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator map factors.

source.place: Corollaries 5.26--5.27, printed p.105; Proposition 7.15 (smoothness of the quotient projection), printed pp.142--143; Theorem 17.9(a), printed p.354 (properness). Smooth connected varieties over an algebraically closed field are geometrically integral, as used throughout Chapter 17; Stacks descent.tex Tag 036D (lemma-regular-local-smooth) for regularity. This is a geometric strengthening for an already represented quotient, not its construction.

proof.text:
Identify the given quotient with the separated finite-type quotient supplied by [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient]. On a test scheme, choose fpqc-local lifts to $G$ for a point of either quotient and send each lift to its image in the other quotient. Two lifts have ratio in $H$, so their images agree. The fpqc descent statement [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] glues these images uniquely; both composites are the identity on the covers by lifts, hence globally. Thus $X$ is separated and of finite type. The same descent constructs its left $G$-action: $a\cdot p(b)=p(ab)$, since $(ab)^{-1}(ab')=b^{-1}b'$. The group laws hold on lifts and hence by uniqueness. The coset criterion on every test scheme gives the kernel-pair isomorphism
$G\times_FH\xrightarrow{\sim}G\times_XG$, $(b,h)\mapsto(b,bh)$,
with inverse $(b,b')\mapsto(b,b^{-1}b')$. Membership of the ratio in $H$ gives its unique factorization through the closed subgroup. These formulas are natural in the test scheme, so they give inverse scheme morphisms.

source.place: Definition 5.20, Propositions 5.21--5.24, pp.104--105; Stacks descent.tex Tag 023Q, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms

proof.text: Base change $p$ along itself. The preceding isomorphism identifies that base change with $G\times_FH\to G$, the base change of the smooth structure morphism of $H$. It is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. Since $p$ is flat, surjective and quasi-compact (indeed of finite presentation), [lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent] descends this smoothness and proves that $p$ is smooth. Independently, $G\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is smooth and factors as $p$ followed by the structure map of $X$. The flat, surjective, locally finitely presented source-descent theorem [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] therefore proves that $X\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is smooth.

source.place: Corollary 5.26, p.105; Proposition 7.15 and its cartesian square, pp.142--143; Stacks descent.tex Tags 02VL and 05B5

proof.text: The continuous surjection $p$ sends the nonempty connected space $G$ onto $X$, so $X$ is nonempty and connected: a decomposition into clopen sets pulls back to such a decomposition of $G$, and surjectivity detects emptiness. Apply [lem-weil-separably-closed-geometrically-connected] to each of $G,H,X$; an algebraically closed field is separably closed. They remain nonempty and connected after every field extension $K/F$. Their structure maps remain smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change], so [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] makes every such base change regular. Apply [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral] to obtain integrality for every $K$, proving geometric integrality. At $K=F$ this proves regularity too. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $G$ and $X$ Noetherian, since they are finite type over the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}F$ (a field has only the two ideals). Locally Noetherian plus quasi-compact gives the stated finite Noetherian affine cover by choosing affine neighbourhoods and taking a finite subcover. The same argument gives geometric integrality for any smooth connected affine finite-type $F$-group, without using any properness assertion.

source.place: Tags 0363 (lemma-separably-closed-field-connected-components), 056S (lemma-smooth-regular); properties.tex Tags 0569 and 033N; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$, put $k=\kappa(x)$, and choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/k$. The fibre $Y_\Omega=G\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is nonempty by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], and finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], since $p$ is of finite presentation. By the density of closed points [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], it has an $\Omega$-point $b$. The kernel-pair formulas of step 1 give an isomorphism $H_\Omega\to Y_\Omega$, $h\mapsto bh$, with inverse $b'\mapsto b^{-1}b'$. Thus $Y_\Omega$ is connected by step 3. The algebraically closed extension criterion [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure] proves that $G_x$ is geometrically connected. This applies to every $x$. Together with smoothness of $p$, [lem-trf-smooth-connected-fibre-normal-integrality] proves that $G\times_X\operatorname{Spec}L$ is integral for every extension $L/k$. Its nonemptiness also follows by base changing the surjection $p$. No $L$-rational lift was assumed: the lift was chosen only over $\Omega$.

source.place: Proposition 5.24, p.104, Corollary 5.27, p.105; Stacks varieties.tex algebraically closed extension criterion; more-morphisms.tex Tag 057J, smooth specialization

proof.text: Now assume $H$ is maximal smooth connected solvable. Among all smooth connected solvable closed subgroups of $G$, choose $B_0$ of largest dimension $d_0$. This set is nonempty (the identity subgroup), and its dimensions are nonnegative integers bounded by $\dim G<\infty$: finiteness is [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], and for a proper subgroup the bound follows from [lem-wf-affine-dimension-drop], since $G$ is an integral affine variety by step 3. These subgroups are integral by the same argument. Apply [lem-sfb-solvable-subgroup-flag-realization] to $B_0\subseteq G$. Obtain a faithful representation on $V$ and a complete flag $\mathcal F_0$ with scheme-theoretic stabilizer exactly $B_0$, as well as the projective finite-type flag scheme $\operatorname{Fl}(V)$. For every flag $\mathcal E$ with stabilizer $K$, that node also gives a smooth connected solvable closed subgroup $K_{\mathrm{red}}^\circ\subseteq G$ with $\dim K_{\mathrm{red}}^\circ=\dim K$. Maximality of $d_0$ therefore implies $\dim K\leq d_0$.

source.place: Theorem 17.9 proof, p.354, first paragraph (maximum dimension and flag realization)

proof.text: The flag scheme is proper, hence separated, by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. Its $G$-action sends each flag subbundle to its image under the representation matrix; the group laws are the matrix action laws. Let $O_0$ be the reduced orbit of $\mathcal F_0$ in $\operatorname{Fl}(V)$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry], it is smooth and locally closed, of dimension $\dim G-d_0$. The same node and step 5 show that every orbit of an $F$-rational flag has dimension $\dim G-\dim K\geq\dim G-d_0$. If the boundary $\overline{O_0}\setminus O_0$ were nonempty, it would be a nonempty closed subset of the finite-type flag scheme. The Jacobson density lemma and the closed-point residue-field lemma supply an $F$-rational point in it. But its orbit has strictly smaller dimension than $O_0$ by the orbit lemma, contradicting this lower bound. Thus $O_0$ is closed. It is proper and finite type by the closed-reduced-subscheme clause of [lem-sfb-solvable-subgroup-flag-realization]. Finally [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry] identifies $G/B_0$ with $O_0$, respecting $b\mapsto b\mathcal F_0$, and says that every $F$-point lifts to $G(F)$.

source.place: Theorem 17.9 proof, p.354, second paragraph; orbit lemma 1.66 and Propositions 7.11--7.12, pp.141--142

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-solvable-proper-fixed-point] to the left action of $H$ on the nonempty proper finite-type scheme $O_0\simeq G/B_0$. Write its fixed point as $g\mathcal F_0$ with $g\in G(F)$, using step 6. Being scheme-theoretically fixed means, on every $F$-algebra $A$, that $g^{-1}hg$ stabilizes $(\mathcal F_0)_A$ for every $h\in H(A)$. Its scheme-theoretic stabilizer is $B_0$, hence $H\subseteq gB_0g^{-1}$ as subgroup schemes. The latter subgroup is smooth, connected and solvable, since conjugation is a group-scheme isomorphism. Maximality of $H$ makes this inclusion an equality. The formulas
$aH\mapsto agB_0$ and $cB_0\mapsto cg^{-1}H$
give inverse quotient maps: replacing $a$ by $ah$ changes $ag$ by right multiplication with $g^{-1}hg\in B_0$, and replacing $c$ by $cb$ changes $cg^{-1}$ by right multiplication with $gbg^{-1}\in H$. On fpqc-local lifts these formulas are scheme morphisms and agree on overlaps, so [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] glues them; their composites are the identity. Quotient uniqueness in step 1 identifies the first quotient with the given $X$. Thus $X\simeq G/B_0\simeq O_0$ is proper over $F$.

source.place: Theorem 17.9 proof, p.354, final paragraph (fixed point, conjugacy and completeness)

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q17-895789ddf (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all 22 cited statements in full; there are no new nodes and the statement is unchanged. The proof follows Milne iAG2017 Thm 17.9(a), p.354, which I checked in the local PDF: B0 of maximum dimension, a flag with stabilizer B0, the minimum-dimension orbit closed by 1.66, the flag variety proper, then the Borel fixed point 17.3 gives H<=gB0g^-1 and equality by maximality. Step 1: quotient identification, action and kernel pair by fpqc gluing; elementary and correct. Step 2: p is smooth by 02VL fpqc base descent applied to G x_X G = G x H -> G (p is flat, qc and surjective), and X is smooth by 05B5 source descent. Step 3: 0363, 056S and regular+connected => integral give geometric integrality; finite type over Spec F gives Noetherian. Step 4: an Omega-point via Jacobson density and the residue-field node, Y_Omega = H_Omega, the alg-closure criterion, then 057J-type integrality for every L/kappa(x); no L-point is assumed. Step 5: dimension bounds, and the flag node's K_red° clause handles nonreduced stabilizers in char p. Step 6: boundary F-point contradiction, closed reduced orbit proper, orbit = G/B0. Step 7: fixed point and descent of the coset maps. Edge cases checked: G=H, G=Ga, alpha_p, disconnected H. Not a duplicate of the unsplit general-borel-flag-variety (it lacks the regularity and fibre clauses); no cycle. Batch 5: lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent (02VL) and lem-trf-smooth-connected-fibre-normal-integrality (057J), plus the lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change path, are generic scheme lemmas outside the trace-formula and Poincare-duality content, so they are accepted as tool uses. All declared split_report.tool_uses are generic black-box tools and accepted.

lean.statement: theorem homogeneousQuotient_geometry {F : Type u} [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (G H : Over (Spec (.of F))) [GrpObj G] [GrpObj H] [IsAffine G.left] [Smooth G.hom] [ConnectedSpace G.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] (i : H ⟶ G) [IsClosedSubgroupScheme i] [Smooth H.hom] [ConnectedSpace H.left] (X : Over (Spec (.of F))) (p : G ⟶ X) [Flat p.left] [Surjective p.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation p.left] [QuasiCompact p.left] [QuasiSeparated p.left] (hcoset : ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of F))) (a b : T ⟶ G), a ≫ p = b ≫ p ↔ a⁻¹ * b ∈ Set.range (fun h : T ⟶ H ↦ h ≫ i)) (hlift : ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of F))) (x : T ⟶ X), ∃ (I : Type u) (T' : I → Over (Spec (.of F))) (f : ∀ j, T' j ⟶ T), Presieve.ofArrows (fun j ↦ (T' j).left) (fun j ↦ (f j).left) ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage T.left ∧ ∀ j, ∃ g : T' j ⟶ G, g ≫ p = f j ≫ x) : Smooth G.hom ∧ GeometricallyIntegral G.hom ∧ IsRegularScheme G.left ∧ IsNoetherian G.left ∧ Smooth X.hom ∧ GeometricallyIntegral X.hom ∧ IsRegularScheme X.left ∧ IsNoetherian X.left ∧ Smooth p.left ∧ GeometricallyIntegral p.left ∧ (IsBorelGroupScheme i → IsProper X.hom)

reviewed_lean.note: Every hypothesis and conclusion matches the node. The quotient conditions (Flat/Surjective/LFP/QC/QS, hcoset, hlift with I:Type u) are verbatim the conjuncts of exists_homogeneousQuotient, and X is not assumed separated or of finite type. Conclusions: GeometricallyIntegral (Mathlib geometrically IsIntegral, which includes nonemptiness) on G.hom, X.hom and p.left; IsRegularScheme (with local Noetherianity); IsNoetherian; Smooth. IsBorelGroupScheme -> IsProper X.hom, where IsBorelGroupScheme is the landed def-sfb-borel-subgroup-scheme (closed, smooth, connected, scheme-theoretic solvable, maximal by factorization), equivalent to the node's maximality clause. stmt_deps only gains that landed node (allowed by brief-stage2 §5); statement field verbatim; sorry only; source and blueprint docstrings with all 7 proof steps; all 14 imports exist (Regular arrives through IsRegularScheme); lines <=100; no name clash; no pro-etale content.
